title: Add MSI Titan GT77HX driver wiring and Cooler Boost after 30s sustained 85C
head: 1d4815f3aa6d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: MSI thermal setup is undone later in the same install pass
leads.consequence: On an MSI Intel laptop with model >=42 and a battery, msi.sh disables thermald, then the subsequently sourced Intel leaf installs it and enables thermald.service again. If coolercontrold is installed/enabled (for example separately, given H02), both services are enabled at the next boot despite the conflict-avoidance intent. Without coolercontrold, thermald is still re-enabled contrary to this leaf's intended replacement. The MSI leaf's successful exit does not fix this on reruns, because order is unchanged.

leads.summary: Three requested driver/fan packages are not installable with the called pacman-only helper
leads.consequence: On a normal stock pacman configuration without custom repositories containing these names, r8125-dkms, msi-ec-dkms-git and coolercontrol are in the AUR, not Arch's official repos or the inspected Omarchy stable/rc/edge repository databases. omarchy-pkg-add invokes pacman -S, not the AUR helper. Each error is downgraded to a warning and installation continues with no drivers or fan daemon; on a Titan the watcher cannot find its EC and on a Realtek laptop the blacklist guard will skip. Repeated installs fail the same way.

leads.summary: Existing MSI installations never execute the new hardware leaf during normal update
leads.consequence: The only new caller is omarchy-apply-hardware during ISO setup or manual invocation; omarchy update runs package upgrades and omarchy-migrate but not apply-hardware. No migration is added. Existing GT77HX owners updating normally receive the commands and default unit file but neither the unit installed/enabled nor new hardware setup. A reinstall also only refreshes packages/configs, not hardware. Provide a one-time idempotent hardware migration or an explicitly advertised opt-in path.

leads.summary: The two battery writes actually select 70/80, not the promised 60/80
leads.consequence: When the msi-ec driver supplies these battery attributes and BAT1 is Discharging, writing start=60 calls set_end_threshold(60+10), then writing end=80 calls set_end_threshold(80); the driver's start readback calculates end-10, thus reads 70. Every successful run leaves 70/80, contrary to comment and requirement. Driver has 10-point fixed hysteresis; use its representable 70/80 setting or explain that true 60/80 is unavailable through this interface.

leads.summary: Battery configuration is skipped during the normal AC-powered install and on BAT0
leads.consequence: Even when threshold attributes are present, the script only writes BAT1 while it is exactly Discharging. An MSI laptop with BAT0, or BAT1 currently plugged into AC (Charging/Full/Not charging) skips the only write without warning, with no first-run or update retry. The thresholds retain their previous values. The driver's battery hook attaches attributes to whichever ACPI battery exists, not necessarily BAT1.
leads.triage: partly corroborates F4 (discharging-only); BAT1 hardcode verified by coordinator: msi.sh:54-58 uses BAT1, msi-ec msi_battery_add (msi-ec.c:2123-2130) attaches to every battery

leads.summary: Installing the EC DKMS package does not activate the watcher on this install boot
leads.consequence: On a clean install without msi_ec already loaded, even if msi-ec-dkms-git becomes available, the leaf never calls modprobe. Its package recipe installs /etc/modules-load.d/msi-ec.conf for subsequent boots, while the watcher unit ConditionPathExists requires the module's sysfs entry now. systemctl enable --now can report an enabled unit with its start skipped; this install session has no automatic Cooler Boost until module loading on a future boot. A similar module-loaded-only guard skips the Realtek blacklist and modules-load config on a fresh r8125 install.
leads.triage: overlaps F2 and F1 aside (module-loaded guards during install); not published separately

leads.summary: The systemd unit declares an ordering cycle with its own WantedBy target
leads.consequence: Enabling this normal service creates multi-user.target Wants=watch.service. systemd.target automatically adds target After=each Wanted service (unless the wanted service sets DefaultDependencies=no); this unit additionally sets watch.service After=multi-user.target, yielding contradictory order on boot. Which edge systemd drops or job it removes is manager-specific and untested here, but ordering will not be the requested deterministic start. Remove After=multi-user.target (or order after an actual prerequisite).
leads.triage: contradicted: systemd unit.c unit_add_default_target_dependency skips target After=unit when target is already Before the unit ('Don't create loops'); Opus confirmed no cycle

leads.summary: The promised CoolerControl MSI fan curve has no default control path
leads.consequence: Even if CoolerControl were installed by another route, msi-ec provides a platform sysfs fan_mode and read-only fan-speed attributes, not a hwmon PWM fan controller. CoolerControl 5.0.1 exposes MSI ACPI EC as a *liquidctl* out-of-tree driver. Its AUR daemon recipe lists liquidctl only as an optional dependency and this leaf does not install/configure a corresponding driver. On a stock setup, enabling coolercontrold cannot directly drive the msi-ec fan table as the comment promises; disabling thermald removes that thermal manager without confirming the replacement can control these fans.
leads.triage: overlaps F3 (comment contradicts CoolerControl cannot PWM); liquidctl route not independently verified, not published

leads.summary: New packages are absent from the ISO's outside-base package inventory
leads.consequence: The ISO builder reads this file to stage packages used by setup leaves. Unlike thermald, new r8125-dkms, msi-ec-dkms-git, coolercontrol (and its coolercontrold dependency) and nvidia-settings are not listed. If they become available in a pacman repository, an offline install still has no mirrored copies of the new packages; recording them here is needed in addition to fixing H02. Distinguish names pulled transitively by the builder from entries requested explicitly.

leads.summary: The MSI family detector misses named MSI laptops supported by the proposed EC driver
leads.consequence: A Micro-Star laptop whose product fields use Sword, Leopard, Thin, Delta or standalone GF63/GF65/GF75 names will return 1, so none of the MSI install actions run. Those family strings are present in the msi-ec supported-firmware table, including Sword 17 HX, GP/GL Leopard, GF Thin and Delta 15. Tests enumerate only the selected 14 strings and miss these real inputs. Expand coverage from known MSI model/firmware data or gate setup per actual device capability instead of an incomplete family substring list.
leads.triage: corroborates F7; extra names (Leopard, GF75 Thin) verified in msi-ec.c:132-149

leads.summary: The r8169 blacklist and system unit survive driver/Omarchy removal
leads.consequence: Once r8125 is loaded, the installer writes root-owned /etc/modprobe.d/r8169.conf and /etc/modules-load.d/r8125.conf outside either package's ownership. If r8125-dkms is later removed without deleting these manually installed files, the stock r8169 module remains blacklisted and the requested r8125 module is missing, so RTL8125 Ethernet can be unavailable after reboot. Removing Omarchy likewise leaves an enabled /etc unit whose ExecStart binary no longer exists, and NVIDIA/mkinitcpio drop-ins persist. There is no teardown in this PR. Track ownership or add guarded cleanup that restores the native driver before removal.
leads.triage: dropped: speculative removal lifecycle, low value

leads.summary: An already-running but disabled coolercontrold is left disabled across reboot
leads.consequence: The guard only tests systemctl is-active. If an administrator or another installer started coolercontrold without enabling it, this leaf skips enable --now. It looks correctly configured until reboot, when coolercontrold is absent. Check is-enabled independently (and preserve user choices where appropriate).
leads.triage: dropped: minor is-active vs is-enabled guard, low value

leads.summary: The hardware install test does not execute the install leaf and misses its broken dependencies
leads.consequence: A plausible regression where omarchy-pkg-add remains pacman-only while requested packages are AUR-only, or where thermald is re-enabled in the next leaf, passes every installer assertion because they grep strings in msi.sh and never execute it or the all.sh caller. The test's 'atomic writes' assertion also greps install -Dm644, not atomicity. Add private stubs for package/systemctl/lsmod/mkinitcpio and test the observed final package/unit state and ordering; failures currently provide no feedback.

leads.summary: The polling test treats seven instantaneous invocations as 35 seconds
leads.consequence: A plausible broken watcher that counts calls instead of elapsed wall-clock time satisfies the 'more than 30s sustained' assertions: the six plus one --once invocations run without sleep or a controllable clock. This does not assert thirty seconds have elapsed at all, so a production restart or a quick burst of polls could enable boost early with no failing test. Inject a fake monotonic clock and assert before/after timestamps and reset after downtime.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus F6 E3 (poll counting); not published separately

leads.summary: Developer file-layout vendor list was not updated for new MSI installer
leads.consequence: The contributor guide's hardware-install enumeration still says ASUS / Framework / Intel / Apple / Lenovo quirks and does not name the new MSI hardware leaf; contributors using this file as the supported sibling list will miss the new target. Add MSI beside its siblings.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator: docs/file-layout.md:317 lists ASUS / Framework / Intel / Apple / Lenovo only; published as nit

limits: No physical MSI Titan / firmware was allocated, EC load/thermal and systemd boot behavior were checked against upstream source and unit semantics rather than hardware runtime. Omarchy AUR PKGBUILDs and Arch/Omarchy repository databases are snapshots at hunt time; package availability could change. Other open PRs are unrelated to these issues or add leaves in nonoverlapping install/hardware/all.sh positions; checked #13181, #13299 and #13362 clean three-way text merges, but this is not an integration run.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the Cooler Boost watcher's decision logic matches the description, and both new tests pass at head (45 and 27 checks). The install path does not deliver the feature through Omarchy's own install flow, though. The RTL8125 scan never matches. Three of the packages cannot be installed by `omarchy-pkg-add`. thermald ends up enabled after the same `all.sh` run. The findings below are in order of impact.

### RTL8125 scan in `msi.sh` never matches

`install/hardware/msi.sh:14-15` reads the PCI IDs with `$(< "$device/vendor" 2>/dev/null)`. Bash only treats `$(< file)` as a file read when the substitution has a single `<` redirection (`can_optimize_cat_file` in bash's `builtins/evalstring.c`). With the extra `2>/dev/null`, it becomes an empty command and expands to nothing.

Sandboxed run with bash 5.3, using a fixture file containing `0x10ec` and a fixture `10ec:8125` device:

```text
$(< f)                         -> 0x10ec
$(< f 2>/dev/null)             -> (empty)
msi.sh loop, lines 11-20 as-is -> rtl8125b_found=false
same loop, 2>/dev/null removed -> rtl8125b_found=true
```

**Impact:** `r8125-dkms` is never installed and `r8169` is never blacklisted on any machine. Even with the scan fixed, the blacklist is gated on `lsmod | grep -q r8125`. A freshly built DKMS module is not loaded during installation, so the blacklist branch is skipped there too.

**Suggested change:** drop the two `2>/dev/null` (sysfs PCI devices always have `vendor` and `device`), or follow `bin/omarchy-hw-nvidia` (`shopt -s nullglob` and a plain `$(< …)`). A test that points `OMARCHY_PCI_DEVICES_PATH` at a fixture, as `test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-test.sh` does, would catch this. The same pattern appears in `bin/omarchy-hw-laptop:13` (existing code, outside this PR). Its chassis-type fallback never matches either, though its lid-switch check still works.

### The MSI packages cannot be installed, so the watcher is inert on a fresh install

- `bin/omarchy-pkg-add` only runs `pacman -S`. `r8125-dkms`, `msi-ec-dkms-git` and `coolercontrol` are AUR-only. None of them is in Arch's official repositories or `omacom/omarchy-pkgs`.
- None of the four new packages, including `nvidia-settings`, is listed in `install/omarchy-other.packages`. The ISO builder uses that list to stage packages for offline installs.
- The ISO runs the hardware phase against that offline repository. A stubbed simulation of that flow (Titan DMI, nothing preinstalled) gave:

```text
error: target not found: msi-ec-dkms-git  -> WARNING: Failed to install msi-ec-dkms-git
error: target not found: coolercontrol    -> WARNING: Failed to install coolercontrol
Unit file coolercontrold.service does not exist -> WARNING: Failed to enable coolercontrold
error: target not found: nvidia-settings  -> WARNING: Failed to install nvidia-settings
enabled at the end: omarchy-msi-cooler-boost-watch.service, thermald.service
```

The simulation modelled the offline repository as the package names in the two lists. `r8125-dkms` is missing from the output only because the scan never matches.

With network access, the three AUR packages still fail. `/sys/devices/platform/msi-ec/cooler_boost` comes only from the out-of-tree msi-ec driver. According to the Linux 7.2 source, the in-kernel `msi-ec` (built as a module in linux-omarchy) only adds battery thresholds. It has no `cooler_boost` attribute and no GT77HX firmware entry.

**Impact:** on a fresh install, the watcher unit is enabled but its `ConditionPathExists` never passes, unless the out-of-tree driver is installed some other way. Until then, Cooler Boost is not managed. The live verification in the PR body cannot have come from these install steps: `omarchy-pkg-add` cannot fetch AUR packages, and the r8125 branch never runs.

**Suggested change:** get `msi-ec-dkms-git` (and any other package still needed) into omarchy-pkgs first, then list it in `install/omarchy-other.packages`. The open PR #13181 routes its MSI DKMS driver through omarchy-pkgs first (omarchy-pkgs#623).

### thermald ends up enabled after the same `all.sh` run

```text
all.sh:3   msi.sh             -> systemctl disable --now thermald   (no-op on a fresh install)
all.sh:17  intel/thermald.sh  -> Intel model >= 42 and a battery (i9-13980HX qualifies)
                              -> omarchy-pkg-add thermald
                              -> systemctl enable thermald.service
end state: thermald enabled
```

A stubbed run confirmed this end state both on a fresh install and on a rerun where thermald was already enabled.

**Impact:** the PR's "coolercontrold running with thermald disabled" result is not what `all.sh` produces. Separately, disabling thermald on every Intel MSI laptop reverses the policy in `intel/thermald.sh`, so maintainers need to decide on it. The `msi.sh` comment says coolercontrold "talks to the EC directly and knows the MSI fan table". That contradicts the PR's own statement that CoolerControl cannot PWM these fans.

**Suggested change:** if thermald should stay off on these machines, make `intel/thermald.sh` skip them rather than undoing it later. Otherwise, drop the thermald and CoolerControl steps and keep the watcher.

### Battery thresholds end at 70/80, not 60/80

msi-ec stores one charge limit. Writing `charge_control_start_threshold` sets the end to value + 10, and reading it returns end − 10 (`msi-ec.c`, `charge_control_start_threshold_store`/`_show`; the in-kernel driver uses the same single register). The step writes start 60 and then end 80. It runs only while the battery is `Discharging` and only targets `BAT1`, although msi-ec attaches the attributes to whichever battery exists.

**Impact:** when the step runs, the thresholds end at start 70 / end 80. During a normal install on AC power it is skipped, and machines whose battery is not `BAT1` are skipped too.

**Suggested change:** write only the end threshold (80), note the fixed 10% gap, and find the battery the same way `omarchy-battery-present` does. Not verified on hardware.

### No migration for existing installs

`msi.sh` runs only through `omarchy-apply-hardware`, which runs during ISO setup or when invoked manually. `omarchy update` does not call it, and the PR adds no migration.

**Impact:** existing GT77HX owners get the new commands but no enabled watcher.

**Suggested change:** add a migration that sources `msi.sh`, as recent hardware additions do (`migrations/1787666837.sh`, `migrations/1788862626.sh`).

### Watcher: manual Cooler Boost is switched off, and unreadable sensors read as 0C

Sandboxed `--once` runs against a fixture EC tree:

- With `cooler_boost=on` and both sensors at or below 70C, the next poll writes `off`. The watcher cannot tell its own "on" from someone else's.
- A missing or unreadable temperature file is read as `0`. With the CPU sensor file missing and the GPU at 60C, boost went `on -> off (cpu=0C gpu=60C)`. The failure was simulated with a missing file and with a directory in its place, not with a real EC I/O error.

**Impact:** a Cooler Boost switched on by the user or another tool is turned off within one interval. A read failure on the hot sensor, while the other reads 70C or below, switches boost off and restarts the 30 s window.

**Suggested change:** keep the current state when a sensor cannot be read. Only switch off a boost that the watcher itself switched on, for example by recording that in a state file and reconciling it on start, since `/run` does not survive a reboot.

### `omarchy-hw-msi` accepts some desktops and misses common laptop lines

Checked against real MSI DMI strings from public linuxhw dumps:

| DMI product (family) | Device | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `Creator Z590 P100X` (`Desktop`) | desktop | accepted |
| `Modern ADL-P AM242` (`AIO`) | all-in-one | accepted |
| `GF63 8RC`, `Thin GF63 12HW`, `Sword 15 A11UD` (`GF`) | laptop | rejected |
| `MEG Z490 Trident X`, `MAG Z590 Codex X5` (`Desktop`) | desktop | rejected (correct) |

msi-ec also supports GF75 Thin, GP/GL Leopard and Sword firmwares, which the family list misses. On real MSI laptops, `product_family` is a series name (`GT` for the Titan GT77HX, or `GF`, `GS`, `GE`, `Modern`, `Prestige`), not the full model line used in the test fixtures.

**Impact:** some MSI desktops and all-in-ones get the laptop driver setup, and common laptop lines (GF, Thin, Sword, Leopard) get none of it.

**Suggested change:** match the MSI vendor plus the existing `omarchy-hw-laptop` check instead of a family list. `omarchy-hw-msi-titan` matches the real `Titan GT77HX 13VH` string correctly.

**Optional test improvement:** diagnostic mutants run against the new tests show which changes still pass. Removing the watcher's Titan gate passes both tests. So does ignoring GPU temperature in the polling path, removing the thermald disable or the watcher enable from `msi.sh`, or pointing the unit's `ExecStart` at a missing path. The install assertions grep `msi.sh` text rather than running it, which is also how the RTL8125 scan got through. `docs/testing.md` describes the expected approach: stub `sudo` and the helpers on `PATH`, run the real script, and assert on the call log and the files it writes.

**Smaller notes:**
- `install/` leaf scripts are sourced by `run_logged` and intentionally have no shebang (`agents/skills/install-scripts.md`). `msi.sh` is also the only `install/hardware` leaf that sets `set -euo pipefail`. With `pipefail`, `lsmod | grep -q …` can report failure when `lsmod` gets SIGPIPE. This was shown with a stub `lsmod`; how often the real one hits it was not tested. `[[ -d /sys/module/r8125 ]]` avoids the pipe.
- `/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/10-nvidia-dpms.conf` contains no DPMS option, despite its name. Omarchy runs Hyprland, and SDDM runs on Wayland, so the file only affects an Xorg server, which stock Omarchy does not start.

**Verified:**
- **Watcher logic.** At the default 5 s interval, boost stays off for six polls at or above 85C and turns on at the 7th. Exactly 85C counts, and a dip below 85C resets the counter. At or below 70C it turns off, and 71 to 84C holds the current state. GPU-only heat also turns boost on. A failed EC write is reported and `--once` exits 1, while the daemon keeps polling.
- **msi-ec interface.** The sysfs files the watcher uses match the out-of-tree msi-ec driver: `cooler_boost` on/off, and integer `cpu/` and `gpu/realtime_temperature`. The GT77HX firmwares `17Q2IMS1.107`/`.10D` are in its supported table.
- **Unit file.** `After=multi-user.target` together with `WantedBy=multi-user.target` does not create an ordering cycle. `ExecStart` and the `$OMARCHY_PATH/default/...` source path match how the Omarchy packages install files.
- **Repository checks.** The new commands pass `bin-style-test.sh`, the `test/cli` metadata lint and `privileged-heredoc-test.sh`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** reviewed at head `1d4815f`. None of the changes on current `quattro` affect these findings (the package and hardware-match helpers only gained `--` separators). Source review of the changed files, the hardware install flow, the msi-ec driver (out-of-tree and in-kernel Linux 7.2), AUR and Arch package metadata, the omarchy-pkgs and omarchy-iso build inputs, and public MSI DMI dumps. The PR tests, related repository tests, the watcher and a stubbed run of `msi.sh` followed by `intel/thermald.sh` were executed in a sandbox with fixture DMI, PCI and EC trees and stubbed `sudo`, `pacman`, `systemctl` and `lsmod`. No MSI hardware was available, so real EC behavior, boot-time unit start and the real `lsmod` SIGPIPE rate are untested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
